disagreements.topic: DCF leg: interest tax shield counted twice (the main source of the $44.9-63.7 DCF spread)
disagreements.positions: agent_1 enters EBIT as NOPAT (net income + interest x 0.79) with an after-tax cost of debt (DCF $55.3 at 5.94%). agent_2 (EBIT = NI/1.05 + full net interest, tax -5% to +3%, after-tax Kd) $62.6; agent_3 (EBIT = NI + full interest, tax 0, after-tax Kd 4.27%) $63.7; agent_4 (EBIT = NI/1.10 + interest, tax 0, after-tax Kd) $50.8 at 6.55%; agent_5 (tax -8% to +5% on EBIT incl. full interest, after-tax Kd 4.8%) $44.9 at 6.4%.
disagreements.resolution: With tax 0 on an EBIT that adds back full pre-tax interest, FCFF already carries the interest tax shield; discounting at an after-tax cost of debt counts it again (~21% x $1.7-3.0B = $0.4-0.6B a year, ~20% of steady-state FCFF). Reconciled set uses agent_1's NOPAT form. Re-run on agent_3's own years and 6.1% WACC with EBIT restated to NOPAT, its DCF is $29.8, not $63.7 (engine check). Reconciled DCF $48.0 at 5.93%: EV at the horizon ~1.0x rate base, i.e. returns about equal to a CAPM cost of capital; the market's 17.2x implies a ~5.5% WACC.
disagreements.evidence: Arithmetic in each agent's inputs_detail (EBIT and tax rows) checked against model_engine.py check; interest TTM $1,642M (F67), 2026 +$240-250M [2].

disagreements.topic: WSJ/Anthropic S-1: direct load, backlash and counterparty risk
disagreements.positions: All five: no verified Anthropic load in Xcel territory; indirect demand via Google; S-1 opposition risk visible in MN/CO.
disagreements.resolution: Agreed after my own search: no named source ties Anthropic (or Nscale/Lambda capacity) to an Xcel site. The channel is Google ($111B of Anthropic cloud commitments plus a >$160B TPU lease per the WSJ), which is Xcel's Pine Island ESA counterparty. Backlash is already in the record: the MN AG asks the MPUC not to approve the Google ESA as filed (Oct 1). Counterparty risk sits first on tariff terms (MN 15-year approved tariff; CO large-load tariff filed 2026-04-02 and pending at the CPUC: 15-year contracts, financial assurance in cash or credit and exit fees for loads of 50 MW+ [15]); SPS Texas/New Mexico large-load tariffs were still to be filed per the Q2 call, so that is where shareholders carry more of it.

ipo_liquidity_view: Kilian's question: the Anthropic IPO is unlikely to drain XEL specifically. Nearest base rate: in the SpaceX IPO week of 2026-06-08 XEL closed +0.2% ($79.04 -> $79.22) and XLU +0.4% (Twelve Data, verified), while mega-cap tech bore the selling. XEL's holders are income/utility funds and its moves this year track the 10y (5.12% now vs 4.75% end-July; low $68.72 on Sep 25 at the 5.3% peak). The S-1 is a general demand positive through Google (Xcel's ESA counterparty) and a reminder of organised opposition already visible in MN. Plan: a flow-driven dip to ~$70 (14.6x horizon NTM EPS) with the 10y stable and the Oct-29 plan intact (equity ~40% of increments, 2027 guide around $4.45-4.55) is a legitimate buying opportunity (~7% under fair value plus ~3% yield); a dip driven by the 10y moving toward 5.5% is not, and below $63 re-underwrite. Better entry points are after Oct 29 (equity size known) rather than into the IPO week.
summary: XEL is fairly priced: the reconciled rate-base build (NTM EPS $4.78 at 17.2x) and a consistent driver DCF give $75.2 (ex-dividend) vs $76.68, a ~2% total return plus a ~3.1% yield. The forecasters agree on the business; my checks fixed a DCF error (interest tax shield counted twice by agents 2-4) and a mixed-basis peer median (XEL trades at 0.93x a consistent 18.45x, not 0.91x). The swing factors are the 10y, the Oct-29 equity plan and MN/CO regulation, not the Anthropic IPO, which has no verified link to Xcel's territory. A rates-neutral dip toward $70 is buyable; $63 is the thesis break.
